# Operations

<!-- Generated by `dart run tool/gen_api_docs.dart` in packages/zarvan_api. Do not edit. -->

Non-Flutter operations are available on CLI, MCP, REST and JSON-RPC; Flutter-dependent operations are CLI-only. Read-classified operations do not write project content but can change session or sandbox-world state. Journalled file writes can be undone with `undo.undo`; destructive writes require preview and confirmation. Results are `{ok, data, warnings, diff?, undoId?, durationMs}` or `{ok:false, error:{code, message, hint?}}`.

CLI blocks show command syntax, not complete runnable examples. For registry-backed commands, supply missing parameters via `--args` (JSON object) or `--stdin`, and request `--json` for the result envelope. Discover schemas and examples with `engine.operation`; for legacy or CLI-only commands use `zarvan help`. Stateful `world.*` workflows need a persistent MCP/HTTP process; separate CLI invocations do not share worlds.

## animation

### `animation.clear_events`

Clear frameEvents cues on one frame of a clip JSON file.

Without `type`, clears every cue on the frame. With `type`, removes only matching cues. Undoable.

*write*, needs an open project, idempotent.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | string; required | Project-relative animation clip JSON file. |
| `frame` | integer; required | Zero-based index of the frame to edit. |
| `clip` | string | Clip name when the file contains multiple clips. |
| `type` | string | Optional event cue type to clear; omit to clear every type. |
| `apply` | boolean | Write now (default for write operations) or only preview (default for destructive ones). |
| `confirmation` | string | The token returned by the preview of a destructive operation; applies exactly that change. |

```bash
zarvan animation clear-events <path>
```

REST: `POST /v1/animation/clear_events` · MCP tool: `animation.clear_events` · JSON-RPC method: `animation.clear_events`

### `animation.read`

Load AnimationClip JSON from a project path.

Accepts a single clip object, a name→clip map, or `{ "clips": [ … ] }`. Returns `{ form, clips, names }` where `clips` is name→clip.

*read*, needs an open project, idempotent.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | string; required | Project-relative animation clip JSON file. |

Errors: `not_found`, `validation_failed`.

```bash
zarvan animation read <path>
```

REST: `POST /v1/animation/read` · MCP tool: `animation.read` · JSON-RPC method: `animation.read`

### `animation.set_event`

Attach a frameEvents cue to a clip JSON file.

Ensures `frameEvents` exists, then appends `{type, data}` on `frame` (0-based). With `replaceType: true`, removes existing cues of that type on the frame first. Undoable.

*write*, needs an open project.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | string; required | Project-relative animation clip JSON file. |
| `frame` | integer; required | Zero-based index of the frame to edit. |
| `type` | string; required | Type of the event cue to attach. |
| `clip` | string | Clip name when the file holds more than one clip. |
| `data` | object | Optional cue payload (e.g. {"id":"swing"}). |
| `replaceType` | boolean | Replace existing cues of this type on the frame. |
| `apply` | boolean | Write now (default for write operations) or only preview (default for destructive ones). |
| `confirmation` | string | The token returned by the preview of a destructive operation; applies exactly that change. |

Errors: `not_found`, `validation_failed`, `invalid_params`.

```bash
zarvan animation set-event <path>
```

REST: `POST /v1/animation/set_event` · MCP tool: `animation.set_event` · JSON-RPC method: `animation.set_event`

## asset

### `asset.atlas_regions`

The named regions of one atlas, with their rectangles.

Look the atlas up by the id `asset.index` shows. Region objects are returned as the manifest stores them.

*read*, needs an open project, idempotent.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `atlas` | string; required | Atlas ID returned by asset.index. |

Errors: `not_found`.

```bash
zarvan asset atlas-regions <atlas>
```

REST: `POST /v1/asset/atlas_regions` · MCP tool: `asset.atlas_regions` · JSON-RPC method: `asset.atlas_regions`

### `asset.index`

List the project's atlases, images, audio, data files and prefabs.

Atlases come from `assets/studio_atlases.json` (which gives them an id levels can use as `atlasId`) and from any `X.json` with a `regions` map next to `X.png` (what `zarvan pack-assets` / `asset.pack` writes). Images already part of an atlas are not listed again under `images`.

*read*, needs an open project, idempotent.

```bash
zarvan asset index
```

REST: `POST /v1/asset/index` · MCP tool: `asset.index` · JSON-RPC method: `asset.index`

### `asset.pack`

Pack every image under a directory into one sprite sheet + region manifest.

Recursively loads images under `input`, MaxRects-packs them (with optional resolution tiers via `scales`), and proposes the PNG sheet(s) plus JSON manifest(s) that `SpriteAtlas.fromManifest` reads. Needs an [ImageCodec] on the context (`zarvan_cli` / `zarvan_api` inject one); without it returns `unsupported`. Same behaviour as `zarvan pack-assets`.

*write*, needs an open project, idempotent.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `input` | path; required | Directory of source images (scanned recursively). |
| `outputImage` | path; default `"assets/packed/atlas.png"` | Project-relative path of the packed PNG. |
| `outputManifest` | path | Defaults to outputImage with a .json extension. |
| `padding` | integer; default `2`; 0 to 64 | Pixel padding between packed regions. |
| `maxWidth` | integer; default `2048`; 1 to 16384 | Requested maximum atlas width in pixels. |
| `scales` | string; default `"1.0"` | Comma-separated tiers, e.g. "1.0,0.5,0.25". |
| `maxAttempts` | integer; default `20`; 1 to 100 | Grow-and-retry attempts before giving up. |
| `apply` | boolean | Write now (default for write operations) or only preview (default for destructive ones). |
| `confirmation` | string | The token returned by the preview of a destructive operation; applies exactly that change. |

Errors: `unsupported`, `not_found`, `validation_failed`, `internal`.

```bash
zarvan asset pack
```

REST: `POST /v1/asset/pack` · MCP tool: `asset.pack` · JSON-RPC method: `asset.pack`

## engine

### `engine.capabilities`

List operation groups, unsupported operations and the active restrictions.

Tells a client what to expect before it calls anything: how many operations each group has, which ones exist but are not served here (they need the Flutter SDK), whether the server is read-only and which operations the allow/deny lists hide.

*read*, idempotent.

```bash
zarvan engine capabilities
```

REST: `POST /v1/engine/capabilities` · MCP tool: `engine.capabilities` · JSON-RPC method: `engine.capabilities`

### `engine.docs`

List documentation pages, or return one page as markdown.

With a docs root (`zarvan_api --docs-root` / `OpContext.docsRoot`) reads the local `docs/` tree: omit `page` to list readable `.md` files (drafts under `proposals/` and the studio QA checklist excluded); with `page` returns `{page, markdown, source: local}`. Without a docs root, serves the curated package bundle (`source: bundled`, markdown bodies for `kRemoteDocsPages`) so agents offline still get full pages; `url` / `docsUrl` remain for the site.

*read*, idempotent.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `page` | string | Docs-relative path (`.md` optional), e.g. concepts/ecs. |

Errors: `not_found`.

```bash
zarvan engine docs <page>
```

REST: `POST /v1/engine/docs` · MCP tool: `engine.docs` · JSON-RPC method: `engine.docs`

## graph

### `graph.add_node`

Add a node of a kind; the first node becomes the entry.

The id defaults to `<kind><index>`. Parameters start at the kind's defaults (non-dialogue graphs) and `params` overrides them. Problems with the graph so far come back as warnings.

*write*, needs an open project.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | path; required | Project-relative graph JSON file. |
| `kind` | string; required | Node kind from graph.node_kinds. |
| `id` | string | Optional ID for the new node; defaults to a generated ID. |
| `params` | object | Node parameter values overriding the kind defaults. |
| `x` | number; default `0` | Horizontal canvas position of the node. |
| `y` | number; default `0` | Vertical canvas position of the node. |
| `apply` | boolean | Write now (default for write operations) or only preview (default for destructive ones). |
| `confirmation` | string | The token returned by the preview of a destructive operation; applies exactly that change. |

```bash
zarvan graph add-node <path>
```

REST: `POST /v1/graph/add_node` · MCP tool: `graph.add_node` · JSON-RPC method: `graph.add_node`

Compile a behavior tree or state machine graph to engine JSON.

| `id` | string; default `"fsm"` | Identifier assigned to the compiled state machine. |
| `apply` | boolean | Write now (default for write operations) or only preview (default for destructive ones). |
| `confirmation` | string | The token returned by the preview of a destructive operation; applies exactly that change. |

Errors: `validation_failed`.

```bash

```

REST: `POST /v1/graph/compile` · MCP tool: `graph.compile` · JSON-RPC method: `graph.compile`

## i18n

### `i18n.keys`

Report every i18n key, which locales have it, and placeholder mismatches.

Reads `assets/i18n/<locale>.json` files (flat `{ "key": "text" }` maps — the same shape the studio uses for its own catalogs). Without `locale`, compares every file; with `locale`, that file is checked against the union of keys from all locales. `missing` lists keys absent from a locale; `placeholderMismatches` lists keys whose `{name}` placeholders differ across locales. `ok` is true when both are empty.

*read*, needs an open project, idempotent.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `locale` | string | Focus the missing report on this locale (e.g. fa). |

```bash
zarvan i18n keys
```

REST: `POST /v1/i18n/keys` · MCP tool: `i18n.keys` · JSON-RPC method: `i18n.keys`

### `i18n.set`

Set one key's text in a locale catalog.

Writes `assets/i18n/<locale>.json` (creates the file when missing). Keys are sorted on write so diffs stay stable. Undoable via `undo.undo`.

*write*, needs an open project, idempotent.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `locale` | string; required | Locale identifier matching the catalog filename. |
| `key` | string; required | Translation key to create or update. |
| `text` | string; required | Localized text for the key. |
| `apply` | boolean | Write now (default for write operations) or only preview (default for destructive ones). |
| `confirmation` | string | The token returned by the preview of a destructive operation; applies exactly that change. |

```bash
zarvan i18n set <locale>
```

REST: `POST /v1/i18n/set` · MCP tool: `i18n.set` · JSON-RPC method: `i18n.set`

## idle

### `idle.best_purchase`

The purchase the greedy advisor would make next, with its cost and income gain.

Loads the definition at its starting state (optionally with `owned` counts applied to generators) and asks the same advisor the auto-buyer and balance simulator use. `null` data means nothing adds income.

*read*, idempotent.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | path | Project-relative idle game definition file; alternatively provide json. |
| `json` | json | Inline idle game definition instead of path. |
| `owned` | object | Generator id -> copies already owned. |
| `mainResource` | string; default `"coins"` | Resource ID used for income and balance reporting. |

Errors: `validation_failed`.

```bash
zarvan idle best-purchase <path>
```

REST: `POST /v1/idle/best_purchase` · MCP tool: `idle.best_purchase` · JSON-RPC method: `idle.best_purchase`

REST: `POST /v1/idle/format_number` · MCP tool: `idle.format_number` · JSON-RPC method: `idle.format_number`

### `idle.simulate`

Play an idle game with a deterministic greedy strategy and report its pacing.

Always buys the best-payback purchase, waiting just long enough to afford it, and prestiges any layer when it would give `prestigeAt` times what is held of that layer's currency (higher layers first). Incomplete challenges are played in order unless `playChallenges` is false. Same input, same report. Use it to tune cost curves without playing.

*read*, idempotent.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | path | Project-relative idle game definition file; alternatively provide json. |
| `json` | json | Inline idle game definition instead of path. |
| `days` | number; default `3`; 0.01 to 3650 | Number of in-game days to simulate. |
| `prestigeAt` | number; 0.01 to ∞ | Prestige a layer once its gain is this many times what is held of that layer's currency. |
| `playChallenges` | boolean; default `true` | Start and complete incomplete challenges in definition order. |
| `mainResource` | string; default `"coins"` | Resource ID used for income and balance reporting. |

Errors: `validation_failed`.

```bash
zarvan idle simulate <path>
```

REST: `POST /v1/idle/simulate` · MCP tool: `idle.simulate` · JSON-RPC method: `idle.simulate`

### `idle.state`

The wallet, income and owned counts of an idle game after a simulated stretch of play.

Loads the definition and, when `afterSeconds` is above zero, plays it with the greedy balance simulator for that long (no prestige). Numbers are formatted strings because they exceed a double.

*read*, idempotent.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | path | Project-relative idle game definition file; alternatively provide json. |
| `json` | json | Inline idle game definition instead of path. |
| `afterSeconds` | integer; default `0`; 0 to 31536000 | Number of simulated seconds before reading state. |
| `mainResource` | string; default `"coins"` | Resource ID used for income and balance reporting. |

Errors: `validation_failed`.

```bash
zarvan idle state <path>
```

REST: `POST /v1/idle/state` · MCP tool: `idle.state` · JSON-RPC method: `idle.state`

### `level.lint`

Check a level loads and, optionally, that every entity is reachable from the spawn.

Always checks structure like the engine loader. With `playable:true` it also walks, falls and jumps over the tileMap from the spawn (a positioned entity named with "player" or "spawn") to every other positioned entity - the same heuristic the studio validator uses. A conservative model, not a physics simulation: it can pass a level that needs wall jumps or ladders. With `includeRender:true` and an [ImageCodec] on the context, the result also carries a base64 PNG structural preview (`pngBase64`) — the same image `zarvan lint --render` writes. Without a codec, `includeRender` adds a problem instead of failing the whole call. `ok` is false when something fails; `problems` says what.

*read*, needs an open project, idempotent.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | path | Project-relative level JSON file; alternatively provide json. |
| `json` | json | Inline level JSON instead of path. |
| `playable` | boolean; default `false` | Run the tile-connectivity reachability heuristic in addition to structural checks. |
| `includeRender` | boolean; default `false` | Include a base64 PNG structural preview of the tileMap (needs ImageCodec). |

```bash
zarvan level lint <path>
```

REST: `POST /v1/level/lint` · MCP tool: `level.lint` · JSON-RPC method: `level.lint`

### `quiz.simulate`

Play many rounds with a fixed policy and report the score, stars and pass rate.

`policy` is `always_correct`, `random` (uniform over the options) or `accuracy:<p>`. Round r of a stage is attempt r+1; endless and race use `<seedBase>:<r>`; daily uses `date` plus r days. In a race each question advances the clock by `secondsPerQuestion`. Same inputs, same report. Use it to tune difficulty and the coin economy without playing.

*read*, idempotent.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bank` | path | The bank file in the project (bank.json). |
| `json` | json | The bank inline, instead of a file. |
| `stopwords` | path | Stop-word file (`{"words": [...]}`). |
| `stopWords` | array | Stop words inline. |
| `mode` | json; required | stage, endless, race, daily, or a mode object such as {"type": "endless", "lives": 5}. |
| `author` | string | Stage: the chapter (default: the first author). |
| `tier` | enumeration; one of `easy`, `medium`, `hard`, `literary` | Stage: the tier (default easy). |
| `attempt` | integer; 1 to ∞ | Stage: attempt number; it changes which word is hidden. |
| `date` | string | Daily: the local date, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `seedBase` | string | Endless and race: text the question seeds come from. |
| `policy` | string; default `"always_correct"` | Scripted answer policy: always_correct, random or accuracy:<p>. |
| `runs` | integer; default `100`; 1 to 10000 | Number of rounds to simulate. |
| `seed` | integer; default `1` | Deterministic seed for the simulated answer policy. |
| `secondsPerQuestion` | integer; default `4`; 0 to ∞ | Simulated time per question in race mode. |

```bash
zarvan quiz simulate
```

REST: `POST /v1/quiz/simulate` · MCP tool: `quiz.simulate` · JSON-RPC method: `quiz.simulate`

## release

### `release.build`

Build a signed Android AAB and/or iOS IPA (needs the Flutter SDK; available from the CLI).

Runs `flutter build`. Implemented by `zarvan build-release` because it needs the Flutter SDK and runs for minutes; servers without Flutter list it under `engine.capabilities.unsupported`.

*write*, needs an open project, **CLI only (needs the Flutter SDK)**.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `apply` | boolean | Write now (default for write operations) or only preview (default for destructive ones). |
| `confirmation` | string | The token returned by the preview of a destructive operation; applies exactly that change. |

```bash
zarvan build-release
```

### `release.plan`

Plan an Android or iOS release build (command, files, problems) without running it.

The same planning `zarvan build-release` does: the exact `flutter build` command line, the files it would create (their paths only; contents can hold secrets and are never returned), errors such as a missing signing setup and warnings. Pass the android or ios fields that apply.

*read*, idempotent.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `platform` | enumeration; required; one of `android`, `ios` | Target store platform for the release plan. |
| `target` | string; default `"lib/main.dart"` | Flutter application entry point. |
| `buildName` | string; default `"1.0.0"` | User-visible application version. |
| `buildNumber` | string; default `"1"` | Store build number. |
| `flavor` | string | Optional Flutter build flavor. |
| `keystorePath` | string | Path to the Android signing keystore. |
| `keystorePassword` | string | Password for the Android keystore; supply securely. |
| `keyAlias` | string | Alias of the Android signing key. |
| `keyPassword` | string | Password for the Android signing key; supply securely. |
| `gradleText` | string | Contents of android/app/build.gradle(.kts); checked for key.properties. |
| `teamId` | string | Apple developer team identifier. |
| `exportOptionsPlist` | string | Path to the iOS export options property list. |
| `noCodesign` | boolean; default `false` | Plan an unsigned iOS build. |

```bash
zarvan release plan <platform>
```

REST: `POST /v1/release/plan` · MCP tool: `release.plan` · JSON-RPC method: `release.plan`

## strategy

### `strategy.rules`

Describe the turn-based components, orders, systems and AI kinds the engine ships.

### `strategy.simulate_turns`

Run a headless turn-based skirmish for a few team-turns and return the event log.

Loads a level (`path` or inline `json`) with team/grid/AP/unitStats entities, wires `OrderSystem` + `AITurnSystem` + win/combat, and steps until `turns` team-turns have ended (or someone wins). `ai` selects AggressiveAI or TacticalAI for every team. Uses a TileMap navigator when the level has one; otherwise an open grid sized to the units. Deterministic for the same level + args. Nothing is written.

*read*, idempotent.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | path | Project-relative level file describing the skirmish. |
| `json` | json | Inline skirmish level JSON instead of path. |
| `turns` | integer; default `1` | How many team-turns (TurnEndedEvent) to run before stopping. |
| `ai` | enumeration; default `"aggressive"`; one of `aggressive`, `tactical` | Built-in AI policy for simulated teams. |

Errors: `validation_failed`.

```bash
zarvan strategy simulate-turns <path>
```

### `undo.redo`

Redo the newest undone write (or a given entry).

*write*, needs an open project.

| `apply` | boolean | Write now (default for write operations) or only preview (default for destructive ones). |


### `undo.undo`

Undo the newest write (or a given entry) by restoring the files it changed.

Restores the files of a journal entry to their content before that write. It refuses if a file changed after the entry (so a later edit is not lost) unless `force` is true. An undone entry can be redone.

*write*, needs an open project.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Entry id from undo.list; default the newest not yet undone. |
| `force` | boolean; default `false` | Allow restoring a journal entry despite conflicting file changes. |
| `apply` | boolean | Write now (default for write operations) or only preview (default for destructive ones). |
| `confirmation` | string | The token returned by the preview of a destructive operation; applies exactly that change. |

Errors: `not_found`, `conflict`.

```bash
zarvan undo undo
```
